title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment, but the tool invented a claim that she used psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the false statement in a post-surgery letter to her GP after kidney stone surgery, and she worried it could harm her workers' compensation case. The urologist later apologized and corrected the record, saying she would review how AI was used. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes.

A report by Digital Rights Watch found unregulated AI scribes sometimes record wrong details, such as the incorrect breast in a cancer diagnosis or a false epilepsy history. Australia's medical regulator says doctors must check all AI output, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration is reviewing AI scribes, with findings due in coming weeks and breaches to be acted on. The advocacy group wants an AI Safety Institute to test and approve tools. Ms Green said she would only consent again if she had an established relationship with the doctor.
